summary: Six open issues, seven open PRs. #9 and #10 are byte-equivalent `strip_fragment` implementations serving duplicate issues #3/#4 — keep one, close the other. #11→#12 is a real stack (#12 is based on `feat/csv-library`), not a duplicate. Issue #8 (:443 collapsing) is already fixed on main by merged PR #2 with regression coverage. PR #12's review is stale against its head but both findings are implemented. PRs #26/#27 are seeded experiment/control — keep unmerged.

actions.rationale: Both ask for opt-in fragment-free bookmark identity with current behavior kept as default, differing only in wording (#3 frames it as JSON export, #4 as saved links). They have attracted two independent PRs implementing the identical helper change. Consolidating onto #3 (which also names exporter and CLI agreement) prevents a third parallel attempt.

actions.rationale: Current main already drops default ports: normalize_url skips the port when (scheme, port) is ('http',80) or ('https',443), so https://example.com:443/docs and https://example.com/docs normalize identically. Merged PR #2 'fix: canonicalize default HTTP and HTTPS ports' (Closes #1) introduced this, and tests/test_bookmarks.py retains test_default_ports_share_identity covering :443, :80 and IPv6.

Merged PR #2 (head 54ac978, merge e565ba0) 'fix: canonicalize default HTTP and HTTPS ports', Closes #1

actions.draft: This looks resolved on main. normalize_url already drops default :80/:443, landed in #2 (Closes #1), and tests/test_bookmarks.py has a regression case asserting https://example.com:443/a and https://example.com/a share an identity. Closing — please reopen with a failing example if you still see duplicates.

actions.rationale: Still valid and not covered by any open PR. Worth pairing with the CSV work in #11 so the exporter path is covered too.
